title: Basic Feed Nutrients
text:
Basic Feed Nutrients:
1. Carbohydrates - common source of energy in ruminants. Sources of carbohydrates include forages, roughages, grains and sugars.

Sugars are found in the cells of plants
Starch is the main component of grains

2. Fats - added to the diets to increase energy density. Energy contents are 2.25 times greater than carbohydrates.

Cottonseeds is rich in fat
Soybean is a good source of fat for cattle

Fats are given in moderate amounts as too much fat in the diet can reduce feed intake and may cause scouring.

3. Proteins - essential for maintenance, growth and milk production. Amino acids are the building blocks of life.

Molasses can be added to feed and water
Spent grain is a good source of protein

facts: Carbohydrates are a common source of energy in ruminants.
Sources of carbohydrates include forages, roughages, grains, and sugars.
Sugars are found in the cells of plants.
Starch is the main component of grains.
Fats are added to ruminant diets to increase energy density.
The energy content of fats is 2.25 times greater than that of carbohydrates.
Soybean is a good source of fat for cattle.
Fats must be given in moderate amounts because excess fat in the diet reduces feed intake and may cause scouring.
Proteins are essential for maintenance, growth, and milk production.
Amino acids are the building blocks of life.
Molasses can be added to feed and water.
Spent grain is a good source of protein.
